mainTopic: Writing documents and betrothal on חול המועד, matches decreed by ה׳, and when a rumor is taken seriously
overview: The amud opens by finishing a discussion about washing linen on חול המועד. אביי says linen may be washed, and he rejects בר הידיא's proof from what people did at ים של טבריה. A new משנה then lists documents that may be written on חול המועד, starting with קידושי נשים. The גמרא brings שמואל's ruling that one may betroth on חול המועד lest another man come first. Two proofs for it are pushed off, and a ברייתא from the school of שמואל finally supports it. The גמרא then explains that the worry is that a rival may pray first, since matches are decided by ה׳, as shown by רבא's story and by פסוקים from תורה, נביאים and כתובים. A side teaching says suspicion always has some basis. The גמרא limits this to a rumor that keeps going for a day and a half, with several conditions. Finally a new משנה lists what may not be written on חול המועד: loan documents, ספרי תורה, תפילין and מזוזות. רבי יהודה's view on this continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Only the listed towels may be washed, not other linen
steps.stepSummary: The end of a challenge: the משנה allows washing barbers' towels and similar items, implying that other linen garments may not be washed on חול המועד.
steps.simpleTranslation: '...the towels of barbers.' These items, yes, they may be washed. Other linen garments, no, they may not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a quote from the משנה and drawing an implication from it. That implication challenges the view that linen clothes may be washed on חול המועד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists specific towels that may be washed on חול המועד. If all linen were allowed, why list these towels? So the list seems to mean that other linen garments are forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Barbers' towels, the cloths placed over someone getting a haircut

steps.confusionAlert: This step starts in the middle of a quote. The word הספרים is the last word of a list from the משנה that began on the previous amud.

phrases.english: (The towels) of the barbers.
These, yes; linen garments, no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a challenge that began before this text, against permitting linen garments to be washed.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that linen garments may be washed on חול המועד
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: By listing only certain towels, the משנה implies that other linen items may not be washed.

steps.title: The משנה means towels of any material
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that the משנה is about towels made even of other materials. Linen in general is permitted anyway.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: The משנה is talking even about towels made of other kinds of material.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי defends the view that linen may be washed. He says the משנה's list is not about linen at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The list in the משנה adds a new point: these towels may be washed even when they are made of other materials, not just linen. So the משנה never meant to forbid other linen garments. Linen clothes stay permitted in general.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
Our Mishnah is (speaking) even of other kinds (of material).

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: מַתְנִיתִין אֲפִילּוּ דִּשְׁאָר מִינֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the scope of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The listed towels were linen, and the list meant that only they are allowed.
steps.terutzMaskana: The listed towels are allowed even when made of other materials. Linen garments in general are allowed.

steps.title: בר הידיא saw linen being washed at the Sea of Tiberias
steps.stepSummary: בר הידיא reports that he saw basins of linen clothes brought out to ים של טבריה to be washed on חול המועד.
steps.simpleTranslation: בר הידיא said: I myself saw the Sea of Tiberias, where people brought out basins full of linen garments during חול המועד.
steps.whatsHappening: בר הידיא brings an eyewitness report. It seems to support the view that washing linen on חול המועד is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This proof comes from what people actually did, not from a text. If people openly washed linen on חול המועד, that suggests it was accepted as permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: חול המועד, the intermediate days of the festival

phrases.english: Bar Hedya said:

phrases.aramaic: לְדִידִי חֲזֵי לִי יַמָּהּ שֶׁל טְבֶרְיָה,
phrases.english: I myself saw the Sea of Tiberias,
that they brought out to it basins of linen garments
phrases.notes: They brought the linen to the sea to wash it there.

phrases.english: during the intermediate days of the Festival.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר בַּר הִידְיָא: לְדִידִי חֲזֵי לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the conclusion of step 2 that linen garments may be washed.
steps.raayaObject: That linen garments may be washed on חול המועד
steps.raayaSupportSource: An eyewitness report of what people did at ים של טבריה

steps.title: What people did is not proof of what is allowed
steps.stepSummary: אביי rejects בר הידיא's proof: maybe those people washed linen against the will of חכמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי objected: Who tells us they did it with the approval of חכמים? Maybe they did it without the approval of חכמים.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks the proof from step 3. He does not attack the ruling itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Seeing people do something only shows that they did it. It does not show that חכמים allowed it. So the eyewitness report cannot prove the halacha. Note that אביי himself already allowed linen in step 2. Here he is only rejecting this one proof.
steps.confusionAlert: אביי is not saying linen is forbidden. He is only saying that בר הידיא's story does not prove it is allowed.
steps.whatToRemember: Linen garments may be washed on חול המועד, based on אביי's reading of the משנה. But what ordinary people do in practice is not by itself proof of halacha.

phrases.english: Abaye strongly objected to it:

phrases.aramaic: מַאן לֵימָא לַן דִּבְרָצוֹן חֲכָמִים עָבְדִי,
phrases.english: Who says to us that they acted with the approval of the Sages?
Perhaps they acted without the approval of the Sages.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ אַבָּיֵי: מַאן לֵימָא לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 3.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof from people's practice, not the ruling permitting linen
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: People's practice may have gone against חכמים, so it proves nothing about halacha.

steps.title: Documents that may be written on חול המועד
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה lists documents that may be written on חול המועד: betrothal documents, גיטין, receipts, wills, gift deeds, פרוזבולין, letters of valuation, and letters of support.
steps.simpleTranslation: And these may be written on חול המועד: documents of betrothing wives, bills of divorce, receipts, wills, deeds of gift, פרוזבולין, letters of valuation, and letters of support.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It moves from washing clothes to a new topic: which documents may be written on חול המועד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Writing is normally a kind of work that is limited on חול המועד. This משנה lists documents that may still be written, apparently because each one serves a real and timely need. The גמרא will explain the details of this list next.

keyTerms.meaning: One may write on חול המועד
Receipts for debts that were paid
Documents that keep a loan from being cancelled by שמיטה
Letters of valuation of property by בית דין

phrases.english: MISHNAH: And these may be written on the (intermediate days of the) Festival:
Betrothals of wives, bills of divorce, and receipts.
Wills, (deeds of) gift, and prozbols.
Letters of valuation and letters of sustenance.
phrases.notes: A letter of sustenance is written when someone takes on the duty to support another person, like a stepdaughter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Certain legal documents may be written on חול המועד.

steps.title: The משנה's list of permitted documents concludes
steps.stepSummary: The משנה adds the last items to its list of documents that may be written on חול המועד: חליצה documents, מיאון documents, arbitration documents, court rulings, and official letters.
steps.simpleTranslation: Also allowed: documents of חליצה and of מיאון, documents of arbitration, court rulings, and official letters of the authorities.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה is simply finishing the list it started in the last step. These are more documents that may be written on חול המועד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not a new topic. It is the second half of the list from step 5. All of these are legal or court documents, joined to the earlier items like גיטין and receipts.

keyTerms.meaning: The ceremony that frees a widow (יבמה) from having to marry her late husband's brother
Refusals: a girl married off as a minor declares she does not want to stay married
Arbitration documents, recording how the chosen judges settled a dispute
Official letters of the ruling authorities

steps.whatToRemember: The full list of documents allowed on חול המועד ends here. The גמרא will now look closely at the first item, קידושי נשים.

phrases.english: Documents of chalitza and of refusal,
and documents of arbitration.
Court rulings,
and letters of the authorities.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues and completes the משנה's list from step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חליצה documents, מיאון documents, arbitration documents, court rulings, and official letters may also be written on חול המועד.

steps.title: שמואל permits betrothal on חול המועד
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens with שמואל's ruling that a man may betroth a woman on חול המועד, so that another man does not betroth her first.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: A man is allowed to betroth a woman on חול המועד, because otherwise someone else might betroth her before him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its discussion with a ruling from שמואל: אירוסין is allowed on חול המועד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally we avoid many activities on חול המועד. שמואל gives a reason to allow אירוסין: if the man waits, he may lose the match to someone else. Losing her counts as a real loss, so he does not have to wait.

keyTerms.meaning: To betroth (do אירוסין, the first stage of marriage)
The intermediate days of a festival
Lest another man get to her first

steps.confusionAlert: שמואל permits אירוסין (betrothal), not a full wedding celebration. Do not mix the two up.

phrases.english: GEMARA: Shmuel said:

phrases.aramaic: מוּתָּר לְאָרֵס אִשָּׁה בְּחוּלּוֹ שֶׁל מוֹעֵד,
phrases.english: It is permitted to betroth a woman on the intermediate days of a Festival,
lest another precede him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: מוּתָּר לְאָרֵס אִשָּׁה בְּחוּלּוֹ שֶׁל מוֹעֵד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא's discussion of the משנה with a related ruling about betrothal.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may betroth a woman on חול המועד, lest another man betroth her first.

steps.title: Trying to support שמואל from the משנה's 'betrothal of women'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the משנה backs שמואל: it allows writing 'קידושי נשים' on חול המועד, which seems to mean actual betrothal documents.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say the משנה supports him? It says: 'These may be written on the festival: קידושי נשים.' Doesn't that mean real betrothal documents?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to prove שמואל is right from the words of our משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the משנה allows writing the document a man uses to betroth a woman, then betrothing on חול המועד must be allowed. That would match שמואל exactly.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say this supports him?
Is it not that...? (introduces the proposed reading)

phrases.english: Let us say that it supports him:
"And these may be written on the Festival:
betrothals of women."
Is it not referring to actual documents of betrothal?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to support step 7's ruling from the משנה in step 5.
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's ruling that betrothal is permitted on חול המועד.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's permission to write 'קידושי נשים' on חול המועד, read as actual betrothal documents.

steps.title: No, the משנה means agreement documents
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof: 'קידושי נשים' may mean שטרי פסיקתא, papers recording the money each family promised, as רב גידל taught in רב's name.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it means documents of stipulation, following what רב גידל said in the name of רב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof by giving the משנה's words a different meaning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the משנה is talking about papers that record the families' money promises, it says nothing about actually betrothing on חול המועד. So the proof for שמואל falls away. The גמרא will next quote רב גידל to explain these papers.

keyTerms.meaning: Documents recording the agreed amounts each family gives the couple
In line with רב גידל's teaching

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא does not say שמואל is wrong. It only says this משנה does not prove him right.

phrases.english: No, documents of stipulation,
phrases.notes: Papers listing how much each side promised to give the young couple.

phrases.english: in accordance with what Rav Giddel said that Rav said.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects step 8's proof by reading the משנה differently.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from the משנה, not שמואל's ruling itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed 'קידושי נשים' means actual betrothal documents, but it can mean documents recording the families' financial agreements.

steps.title: רב גידל: marriage money promises bind through words
steps.stepSummary: רב גידל quotes רב: when two families agree how much each gives their child, and the couple then does קידושין, those promises are binding through words alone.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב גידל said in the name of רב: One side asks, 'How much are you giving your son?' 'So much.' 'How much are you giving your daughter?' 'So much.' Once the couple goes ahead and does קידושין, the promises are acquired. These are the things acquired just by speaking.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes רב גידל's teaching to explain the שטרי פסיקתא it just mentioned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a promise needs a formal act of acquisition (קנין) to be binding. Here, once קידושין takes place, the families' spoken promises become binding with no extra act. The משנה allows writing up such an agreement on חול המועד, which says nothing about betrothing then.

keyTerms.meaning: They went ahead and did the betrothal
They acquired; the promises are binding

steps.whatToRemember: The proof for שמואל from 'קידושי נשים' is pushed off. The משנה can mean papers recording marriage money promises, which become binding through words alone once קידושין happens.
steps.whyThisMatters: The rule that these marriage promises become binding without a formal קנין is an important rule in monetary law.

phrases.english: For Rav Giddel said that Rav said:
"How much are you giving to your son?"
"Such and such.
How much are you giving to your daughter?"
"Such and such."
If they arose and betrothed, they have acquired,
phrases.notes: Once the couple does קידושין, the parents' spoken promises become binding.

phrases.english: these are the things that are acquired through speech.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source mentioned in step 9 to support its reading of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Marriage money promises made between families become binding through words alone once the couple does קידושין.

steps.title: A משנה that forbids only marrying seems to support שמואל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that a משנה backs שמואל. The משנה forbids marrying and יבום on the מועד, which seems to mean betrothal is allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us say this supports שמואל: 'One may not marry women on the מועד, neither virgins nor widows, and one may not do יבום, because it is a joy for him.' This implies that betrothing is allowed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new possible proof for שמואל. A משנה lists only marrying and יבום as forbidden, so it seems betrothal is fine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה names marriage (נישואין) and יבום as forbidden, and the reason is the joy they bring. Betrothal is not on the list, so the גמרא reads the silence as permission. That would match שמואל's ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us say it supports him: the opening words of a suggested proof
Marrying (the full marriage, נישואין, when the couple start living together)
Doing יבום: marrying the widow of a brother who died without children
To betroth (אירוסין/קידושין, the first stage of marriage)

phrases.english: Let us say that this supports him:
phrases.notes: 'Him' means שמואל, who allowed betrothal on חול המועד.

phrases.english: One may not marry women on the Festival,
neither virgins nor widows.
And one may not perform levirate marriage,
because it is a joy for him.
This implies: to betroth is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first proof (from 'קידושי נשים') was rejected, the גמרא tries a second proof for שמואל.
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's ruling that one may betroth on חול המועד
steps.raayaSupportSource: A משנה that forbids only marriage and יבום on the מועד, implying betrothal is allowed

steps.title: The משנה may be saying 'needless to say'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. The משנה may mean that betrothal is obviously forbidden, and it adds that even marriage, which is a מצוה, is forbidden too.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה is speaking in a 'needless to say' style. Needless to say betrothal is forbidden, since it is not a מצוה. But even marrying, which is a מצוה, is also forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes off the proof from the משנה. It says the משנה skipped betrothal because betrothal is the more obvious thing to forbid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Marriage is a מצוה because it leads to having children. Betrothal alone does not. So if even marriage is forbidden on the מועד, betrothal surely is, and the משנה did not need to mention it.

keyTerms.meaning: It is speaking in a 'needless to say' style: it names the bigger case and the smaller one is understood
A commandment; here, marriage leading to having children

steps.confusionAlert: Don't flip it around. Here the גמרא says betrothal is the easier case to forbid, because it is not a מצוה. Marriage is the harder case, because it is a מצוה, yet it is still forbidden.

phrases.english: It is speaking in the style of 'needless to say.'
Needless to say, betrothing is forbidden,
since he is not doing a מצוה,
but even marrying as well,
where he is doing a מצוה, is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from the משנה by reading it in a different way.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof is rejected. שמואל's ruling itself is not disproven.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The inference from silence fails. The משנה may leave out betrothal because it is obviously forbidden, not because it is allowed.

steps.title: A ברייתא from the school of שמואל clearly allows betrothal
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא from the school of שמואל that openly allows betrothal on the מועד but forbids marriage, a betrothal feast, and יבום. The proof is accepted.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear what the school of שמואל taught: One may betroth but not marry. One may not make a betrothal feast or do יבום, because it is a joy for him. Learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a stronger proof for שמואל. A ברייתא says outright that betrothal is allowed, and the גמרא accepts it with 'שמע מינה.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike the משנה, this ברייתא does not rely on silence. It directly says 'מארסין' (one may betroth). Only the joyful parts are forbidden: marriage, the feast, and יבום. So שמואל's ruling is supported.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא taught in the study hall of שמואל
Bringing the bride in, meaning full marriage
Learn from it: the proof is accepted

steps.whatToRemember: שמואל's ruling stands: on חול המועד one may betroth, but one may not marry, make a betrothal feast, or do יבום, because those bring a joy of their own.

phrases.english: Come and hear what the school of שמואל taught:
One may betroth, but one may not marry.
And one may not make a betrothal feast,
and one may not perform levirate marriage,
because it is a joy for him.
Learn from this.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the proof from the משנה was rejected, a clearer ברייתא is brought and accepted.
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's ruling that one may betroth on חול המועד
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of the school of שמואל: 'מארסין אבל לא כונסין'

steps.title: Why worry someone else will betroth her if it is already decided in heaven?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions שמואל's reason. שמואל himself taught that every day a heavenly voice declares whose daughter will marry whom, so why fear that another man will come first?
steps.simpleTranslation: Did שמואל really say 'perhaps another will betroth her first'? But רב יהודה said in שמואל's name: every day a heavenly voice goes out and says, 'The daughter of so-and-so is for so-and-so, the field of so-and-so is for so-and-so.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now challenges the reason behind שמואל's ruling. It points to another teaching of שמואל that seems to clash with it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל's reason for allowing betrothal is the fear that another man might betroth her first. But if heaven already decides who marries whom, that fear seems pointless. So the גמרא shows his two teachings seem to contradict each other.

keyTerms.meaning: And did he really say? Opens a challenge from a person's own words
Perhaps another man will come before him

phrases.english: And did שמואל really say
'perhaps another man will come before him'?
But didn't רב יהודה say in the name of שמואל:

phrases.aramaic: בְּכׇל יוֹם וְיוֹם בַּת קוֹל יוֹצֵאת וְאוֹמֶרֶת:
phrases.english: Every single day a heavenly voice goes out and says:
'The daughter of so-and-so is for so-and-so,'
'the field of so-and-so is for so-and-so.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל שֶׁמָּא יִקְדְּמֶנּוּ אַחֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that the ruling has support, the גמרא questions the reason שמואל gave for it.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's reason 'שמא יקדמנו אחר' (perhaps another will betroth her first)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שמואל himself taught that a heavenly voice decides each match ahead of time. If so, no other man could take her, and the worry seems pointless.

steps.title: The real worry: another man may pray first
steps.stepSummary: שמואל's worry is that a rival may use prayer to change the heavenly decree, so the man should do קידושין quickly.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, שמואל meant: perhaps another man will get ahead of him by praying for mercy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 14. שמואל's concern is not about ordinary competition. It is about another man praying to win the woman.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The בת קול announces who is destined for whom, but prayer can change a decree. So the man worries that a rival will pray first and the woman will end up with the other man. That is why he may do קידושין even on the מועד.

keyTerms.meaning: he will get there before him

phrases.english: Rather: perhaps
another man will get ahead of him through prayer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question raised in Step 14.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שמואל feared another man would simply betroth her first, which makes no sense if the בת קול has already decided the match.
steps.terutzMaskana: The fear is that another man's prayer could change the decree, so a quick קידושין protects the match.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how the גמרא fits the idea that matches are decreed in Heaven together with the power of prayer.

steps.title: רבא and the man who prayed for a specific woman
steps.stepSummary: A story shows that people do pray for a specific woman. רבא warns that such prayer can backfire.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא heard a man praying, 'Let so-and-so be granted to me.' רבא told him not to pray that way: if she is right for you, you will not lose her, and if not, you will end up denying ה׳. Later רבא heard the same man praying that either he or she should die first. רבא said to him, 'Didn't I tell you not to pray about this?'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a story that backs up the answer in Step 15. Real people did pray to win a particular woman.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story shows that praying for a specific match was a real thing, which makes שמואל's worry realistic. It also teaches a lesson: forcing a match through prayer can end badly, because the man later wished one of them dead.

keyTerms.meaning: may she be granted to me

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not saying prayer is useless. Step 15 just said prayer can work. He is warning that forcing a match that was not meant to be can end badly.

phrases.english: Like that incident in which Rava heard
a certain man praying for mercy
and saying: May so-and-so be granted to me.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: לָא תִּיבְעֵי רַחֲמֵי הָכִי.
phrases.english: He said to him: Do not pray this way.

phrases.aramaic: אִי חַזְיָא לָךְ — לָא אָזְלָא מִינָּךְ,
phrases.english: If she is right for you, she will not go away from you,
and if not, you will come to deny God.
Afterward, he heard him saying:
Either let him die before her,
or let her die before him.
phrases.notes: By now he had married her, and things had gone so badly that he wanted out.

phrases.english: He said to him: Did I not tell you
not to pray about this matter?

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי הָא דְּרָבָא שַׁמְעֵיהּ לְהָהוּא גַּבְרָא דְּבָעֵי רַחֲמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Illustrates the answer of Step 15 with a real incident.
steps.raayaObject: The answer that people pray to win a particular woman.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of רבא and the man who prayed.

steps.title: A match is from ה׳: proof from תורה, נביאים and כתובים
steps.stepSummary: רב quotes רבי ראובן בן אצטרובילי that a woman is matched to a man by ה׳, and proves it from three פסוקים.
steps.simpleTranslation: So said רב in the name of רבי ראובן בן אצטרובילי: from the תורה, the נביאים and the כתובים we learn that a woman is matched to a man by ה׳. From the תורה: 'The thing comes from ה׳.' From the נביאים: 'His father and mother did not know that it was from ה׳.' From the כתובים: 'House and wealth are inherited from fathers, but a sensible wife is from ה׳.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up רבא's words, 'if she is right for you, she will not go away,' with a teaching that matches come from ה׳.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'הכי' ('so said') ties this teaching to רבא's point. Each part of תנ״ך gives a פסוק showing that ה׳ arranges marriages: רבקה with יצחק, שמשון's wife, and the sensible wife in משלי.

keyTerms.meaning: a woman is matched to a man by ה׳

steps.whatToRemember: A match is from ה׳, and this is taught in all three parts of תנ״ך. This is the basis for רבא's warning and for the idea of a decreed match.

phrases.english: So said Rav in the name of
Rabbi Reuven ben Itztrobili:

phrases.aramaic: מִן הַתּוֹרָה וּמִן הַנְּבִיאִים וּמִן הַכְּתוּבִים
phrases.english: From the Torah, from the Prophets and from the Writings we learn
that a woman is matched to a man by God.
From the Torah, as it is written:
"Then Lavan and Besuel answered and said:
The thing comes from God."
From the Prophets, as it is written:

phrases.aramaic: ״וְאָבִיו וְאִמּוֹ לֹא יָדְעוּ כִּי מֵה׳ הִיא״.
phrases.english: "But his father and mother did not know that it was from God."
From the Writings, as it is written:
"House and wealth are an inheritance from fathers,
but a sensible wife is from God."

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי אָמַר רַב מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי רְאוּבֵן בֶּן אִצְטְרוֹבִילִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a scriptural source for רבא's statement that a destined match will not be lost.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's words that a destined wife will not go away, and the idea that matches are decreed.
steps.raayaSupportSource: פסוקים from בראשית, שופטים and משלי.

steps.title: Suspicion usually has some basis
steps.stepSummary: Another teaching of רבי ראובן בן אצטרובילי: a person is not suspected of something unless there is some basis, even if only that he was happy when others did it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב also said in the name of רבי ראובן בן אצטרובילי (some say it was taught in a ברייתא): A person is not suspected of something unless he did it. If he did not do all of it, he did part of it. If he did not do part of it, he thought about doing it. If he did not even think about doing it, he saw others do it and was happy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another teaching from the same teacher just quoted. This starts a new side topic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not connected to the laws of the מועד. It appears here only because רבי ראובן בן אצטרובילי was just quoted. The teaching goes down step by step: did it fully, did part, thought about it, or was happy when others did it. Suspicion always has some root.

keyTerms.meaning: thought about it in his heart
it was taught in a ברייתא

steps.whyThisMatters: This teaching lays the groundwork for the coming discussion about suspicion, and the גמרא will soon question it.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַב מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי רְאוּבֵן בֶּן אִצְטְרוֹבִילִי,
phrases.english: And Rav said in the name of Rabbi Reuven ben Itztrobili,
and some say it was taught in a baraita,
Rabbi Reuven ben Itztrobili said:
A person is not suspected of something
unless he did it,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם לֹא עָשָׂה כּוּלּוֹ — עָשָׂה מִקְצָתוֹ,
phrases.english: and if he did not do all of it, he did part of it,
and if he did not do even part of it,
he thought in his heart about doing it,
and if he did not even think in his heart about doing it,
he saw others who did it and was happy.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי רְאוּבֵן בֶּן אִצְטְרוֹבִילִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A side topic, linked only because the same teacher was quoted in Step 17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Suspicion against a person always has some basis, even if only that he was happy when others did the wrong.

steps.title: Challenge from a verse: Israel made up false things about God
steps.stepSummary: רבי יעקב challenges the rule from a פסוק saying the Jewish people made up untrue things about ה׳.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יעקב raised an objection: "And the children of Israel made up things that were not true against ה׳ their God." This shows people can invent completely baseless accusations.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יעקב attacks the rule from Step 18 using a פסוק. The פסוק shows people saying false things with no basis at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 18 said nobody is suspected unless there is some basis. Here people said things about ה׳ that were completely untrue, and there can be no real basis for that. So it seems people can accuse with no basis at all.

keyTerms.meaning: they made up / fabricated (things in secret)
that were not true / not right

phrases.english: Rabbi Ya'akov raised an objection:
"And the children of Israel fabricated
matters that were not right
against ה' their God"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rule taught in Step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי ראובן בן אצטרובילי's rule that no one is suspected without some basis.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק shows a completely baseless accusation against ה׳, so suspicion without basis does happen.

steps.title: Answer: they only said it to anger God
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that Israel did not really believe their words; they said them to anger ה׳.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, they did it to anger ה׳.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רבי יעקב's challenge. That case was not real suspicion at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule in Step 18 is about people who actually suspect someone. In the פסוק, the people knew their words were false and said them only to provoke ה׳. So it does not show that true suspicion can arise from nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: that is why they did it

phrases.english: There, it was to anger [God] that they did it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case: a deliberate provocation, not real suspicion.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק seemed to show real suspicion with no basis.
steps.terutzMaskana: They knowingly spoke falsely to anger ה׳, so this is not suspicion and the rule stands.

steps.title: Challenge: the men of Israel suspected משה
steps.stepSummary: A second challenge: according to רב שמואל בר יצחק, every man warned his wife not to be alone with משה, suspecting someone completely innocent.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: "And they were jealous of משה in the camp, of אהרן the holy one of ה׳." רב שמואל בר יצחק said: This teaches that each man warned his wife against being alone with משה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second challenge to the rule. It uses a פסוק as explained by רב שמואל בר יצחק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: משה was certainly innocent, yet the men suspected him with their wives. This seems to show that a person can be suspected with no basis at all.

keyTerms.meaning: he gave a formal warning of jealousy to his wife

phrases.english: Come and hear:
"And they were jealous of Moses in the camp,
of Aaron, the holy one of ה'",
Rav Shmuel bar Yitzchak said:
This teaches that each one
warned his wife regarding Moses!
phrases.notes: He means each husband told his wife not to be alone with משה, as if he suspected them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second challenge to the rule of Step 18, after the first was answered.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that no one is suspected without some basis.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: משה was completely innocent, yet the men suspected him, so suspicion can arise with no basis.

steps.title: Answer: they acted out of hatred
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the men did not truly suspect משה; they acted out of hatred to put him down.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, it was out of hatred that they did it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the second challenge. Again, this was not real suspicion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The men did not actually believe משה did anything wrong. They hated him and wanted to shame him. Since this was not real suspicion, the rule from Step 18 still holds.

phrases.english: There, it was because of hatred that they did it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 21 the same way Step 20 answered Step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case: hostility, not real suspicion.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The men really suspected משה with no basis.
steps.terutzMaskana: They acted out of hatred, not real suspicion, so the rule stands.

steps.title: Challenge from רבי יוסי and רב פפא: innocent people are suspected
steps.stepSummary: A third challenge: רבי יוסי prays to share the portion of someone suspected while innocent, and רב פפא says he himself was suspected while innocent.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רבי יוסי said, "May my portion be with someone who is suspected of something and did not do it." And רב פפא said, "They suspected me, and I had not done it!"
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a third challenge, this time from sages instead of פסוקים. Both statements describe real suspicion of innocent people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This challenge is stronger than the first two. These are real cases of suspicion, not provocation or hatred, and רב פפא is speaking about himself. So the earlier answers will not work here.

keyTerms.meaning: my portion (my share in the World to Come)
and it is not in him (he is innocent)

phrases.english: Come and hear: Rabbi Yosei said:
May my portion be with one
whom they suspect of something, and it is not in him.
And Rav Pappa said:
They suspected me, and it was not in me!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third challenge to the rule of Step 18, after the first two were answered.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that no one is suspected without some basis.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוסי assumes innocent people do get suspected, and רב פפא testifies it happened to him, so suspicion can exist with no basis.

steps.title: Answer: a rumor that stops versus one that keeps going
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא resolves the contradiction: a rumor that dies down can be baseless, but a rumor that keeps going has some basis.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. This is about a rumor that stops; that is about a rumor that does not stop.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the third challenge by splitting the cases into two kinds of rumors.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי and רב פפא are talking about a rumor that dies down, which can be completely false. The rule of רבי ראובן בן אצטרובילי is about a rumor that keeps going. A lasting rumor shows there is some basis behind it. So both sides are true, each in its own case.

keyTerms.meaning: it is not difficult (two sources can be reconciled)

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא does not say which "הא" is which. The rumor that stops goes with רבי יוסי and רב פפא (an innocent person can be suspected). The rumor that does not stop goes with רבי ראובן בן אצטרובילי's rule (there is some basis).

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
This is with a rumor that stops,
phrases.notes: This is the case of רבי יוסי and רב פפא, where an innocent person can be suspected.

phrases.english: that is with a rumor that does not stop.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 23 by splitting the cases.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (הא בכך הא בכך).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Suspicion of innocent people seemed to contradict the rule that there is always some basis.
steps.terutzMaskana: A short-lived rumor can be baseless. A rumor that does not stop shows some basis.
steps.whyThisMatters: This gives a practical way to judge rumors: a rumor that dies down should not be held against a person.

steps.title: How long must a rumor last?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how long a rumor must continue to count as one that "does not stop."
steps.simpleTranslation: And a rumor that does not stop: for how long?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a follow-up question to define the new distinction. This sets up אביי's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying "a rumor that does not stop" is not enough on its own; we need a measure. The גמרא wants to know how much time makes a rumor count as lasting.

keyTerms.meaning: until how much / for how long

phrases.english: And a rumor that does not stop: for how long?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the definition of a term introduced in Step 24.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The length of time a rumor must last to count as "not stopping."

steps.title: אביי: town gossip lasts a day and a half
steps.stepSummary: אביי reports from the woman who raised him that local gossip lasts a day and a half.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: My nurse told me, town gossip lasts a day and a half.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the question with a time measure he learned from the woman who raised him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Ordinary gossip in a town lasts about a day and a half and then fades. If a rumor keeps going beyond that, it counts as one that "does not stop," which shows there is some basis behind it.

keyTerms.meaning: literally "mother"; here, the nurse who raised אביי
the talk / gossip of the town

steps.whatToRemember: A person is not suspected without some basis, but only when the rumor does not stop (lasting beyond a day and a half). A rumor that dies down can be totally false, as רבי יוסי and רב פפא show.

phrases.english: Abaye said: My mother told me:
phrases.notes: This is not his real mother; אביי often quotes the woman who raised him this way.

phrases.english: The gossip of the town lasts a day and a half.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 25.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Ordinary town gossip lasts a day and a half; a rumor lasting longer counts as one that does not stop.

steps.title: A rumor that stopped in the middle does not count
steps.stepSummary: The day-and-a-half rule only applies if the rumor kept going without a break. If it stopped in between, we ignore it.
steps.simpleTranslation: This rule only applies when the rumor did not stop during that time. If it did stop in between, we have no problem with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a limit to אביי's day-and-a-half rule. The rumor has to run nonstop to be taken seriously.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 24 said a rumor that keeps going has some basis. Now we learn what 'keeps going' means: it must run the full day and a half with no break. A break shows the rumor died out, so it is treated as baseless.

keyTerms.meaning: These words apply only... (a phrase that limits a rule)
We have no problem with it

phrases.aramaic: וְהָנֵי מִילֵּי דְּלָא פְּסַק בֵּינֵי בֵּינֵי,
phrases.english: This applies only when it did not stop in between,
phrases.notes: 'It' is the rumor. 'In between' means during אביי's day and a half.

phrases.english: but if it stopped in between,
we have no problem with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָנֵי מִילֵּי דְּלָא פְּסַק בֵּינֵי בֵּינֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits אביי's day-and-a-half measure to a rumor with no break.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only a rumor that runs nonstop for a day and a half is treated as having some basis.

steps.title: A stop caused by fear does not count as a stop
steps.stepSummary: A break only clears the person if people stopped talking on their own, not because they were afraid of him.
steps.simpleTranslation: When the rumor stopped in between, we only said it is baseless if it did not stop out of fear. If it stopped because people were afraid, the rule does not apply.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא limits the rule from Step 27. A break caused by fear does not clear the person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If people went quiet because they were scared of the person, the rumor did not really die out. It only went quiet. So the rumor is still treated as having some basis.

keyTerms.meaning: We only said this when... (a phrase that limits a rule)

phrases.english: And when it stopped in between,
we only said this
when it did not stop out of fear,
but if it stopped out of fear,
not.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי פְּסַק בֵּינֵי בֵּינֵי, לָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a limit to the 'stopped in between' rule from Step 27.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A break caused by fear does not make the rumor baseless.

steps.title: A rumor that started up again does not count as stopped
steps.stepSummary: A break only clears the person if the rumor did not come back afterward.
steps.simpleTranslation: We only said a stopped rumor is baseless if it did not spring up again. If it sprang up again, the rule does not apply.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second limit on the 'stopped' rule. If the rumor came back, the break does not help.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once a rumor comes back, the earlier pause is cancelled. The rumor is treated as one that keeps going, so it has some basis.

keyTerms.meaning: It sprouted again, meaning the rumor came back

phrases.english: And we only said this
when it did not sprout again,
phrases.notes: Literally 'sprout,' like a plant. Here it means the rumor started up again.

phrases.english: but if it sprouted again, not.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא אֲמַרַן, אֶלָּא דְּלָא הָדַר נָבֵט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second limit on when a stopped rumor counts as baseless.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the rumor came back after stopping, the break does not clear the person.

steps.title: If the person has enemies, even a nonstop rumor is dismissed
steps.stepSummary: A rumor that keeps going is only taken seriously if the person has no enemies. If he has enemies, we assume they spread it.
steps.simpleTranslation: We only said a nonstop rumor must be taken seriously when he has no enemies. If he has enemies, it is the enemies who put out the rumor.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a final limit, this time on the nonstop rumor. Known enemies explain why the rumor keeps going.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now, a nonstop rumor meant there was some truth to it. But if the person has enemies, there is another reason the rumor keeps going: they keep spreading it. So it does not show he did anything wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: They put out the rumor, meaning they started and spread it

steps.whatToRemember: A rumor is taken seriously only when all four are true: it lasted a day and a half; it had no real break (a break caused by fear does not count); it did not come back after a break; and the person has no enemies who could be spreading it.

phrases.english: And we only said this
phrases.notes: This one goes back to the rumor that does NOT stop, the kind that is normally taken seriously.

phrases.english: when he has no enemies,
but if he has enemies,
it is the enemies who put out the rumor.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא דְּלֵית לֵיהּ אוֹיְבִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from limits on the stopped rumor to a limit on the nonstop rumor.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A nonstop rumor about someone with enemies is blamed on the enemies, not taken as proof.

steps.title: No writing loan documents on חול המועד, with two exceptions
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה forbids writing loan documents on חול המועד. It allows it if the lender does not trust the borrower, or if the scribe has nothing to eat.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: One may not write loan documents on חול המועד. But if the lender does not trust the borrower, or the scribe has nothing to eat, he may write it.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins after the side discussion about rumors. It goes back to the topic of writing on חול המועד from Step 5. This time it lists what may NOT be written, starting with loan documents.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Writing a loan document is work that can usually wait until after the יום טוב. The משנה allows two exceptions. If the lender does not trust the borrower, he could lose his money without a document. If the scribe has nothing to eat, he needs to earn money now.

keyTerms.meaning: חול המועד, the in-between days of the יום טוב

phrases.english: MISHNA:
One may not write loan documents on חול המועד.
But if he does not trust him,
phrases.notes: The lender does not trust the borrower, and worries he will later deny the loan.

phrases.english: or if he has nothing to eat,
phrases.notes: This is the scribe, who needs the pay.

phrases.english: he may write.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ אֵין כּוֹתְבִין שְׁטָרֵי חוֹב בַּמּוֹעֵד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the rumor discussion has ended, continuing the topic of writing on חול המועד from Step 5, but now listing what is forbidden.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Loan documents may not be written on חול המועד unless the lender does not trust the borrower or the scribe has nothing to eat.

steps.title: No writing or correcting ספרים, תפילין, or מזוזות on חול המועד
steps.stepSummary: The משנה forbids writing ספרי תורה, תפילין, and מזוזות on חול המועד. One may not even fix one letter, even in ספר עזרא.
steps.simpleTranslation: One may not write ספרים, תפילין, or מזוזות on חול המועד. One may not correct even one letter, even in the ספר of עזרא.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves on to writing holy texts. It forbids writing them on חול המועד, and even forbids small corrections.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even fixing one letter is forbidden. That holds even for ספר עזרא, the most important ספר תורה. So the ban covers the smallest act of writing, even in the most important ספר.

phrases.english: One may not write scrolls,
תפילין, or מזוזות on חול המועד,
and one may not correct a single letter
even in the scroll of עזרא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה, moving from loan documents to holy texts.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ספרים, תפילין, and מזוזות may not be written or even corrected on חול המועד.

steps.title: רבי יהודה lets a person write תפילין and מזוזות for himself
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה disagrees with the first opinion. He allows a person to write תפילין and מזוזות for his own use.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: A person may write תפילין and מזוזות for himself.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה gives a different opinion from the first part of the משנה. His statement keeps going past this point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion banned writing תפילין and מזוזות completely. רבי יהודה allows it when the person writes them for himself. Note that he mentions only תפילין and מזוזות, not ספרי תורה.
